reviews.frank_statement: FRANK should be represented as heterogeneous interacting loops with typed budgets, state and halt/continue/escalate semantics.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Ordinary event-driven orchestration plus existing generic control flow is sufficient and explicit loop representation adds no semantic value.
reviews.falsifier: H1/H2 differential replay shows loop identity/budget/halt receipts add no recoverable semantic or diagnostic information over ordinary scheduling.

reviews.frank_statement: Coupled loops can be lowered without explicitly declaring within-epoch read/order semantics.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Scheduler iteration order is harmless implementation detail.
reviews.falsifier: Permutation testing of an unordered/set-like loop family remains semantically equivalent under in-place lowering.

adversarial_checks: Replacing snapshot reads with in-place reads caused schedule-order dependence
reviews.reason: For the tested unordered/set-like coupled loop class, in-place reads changed semantics with iteration order.
reviews.claycode_action: Require explicit scheduling class: snapshot/set-like vs ordered/sequential/asynchronous; do not silently infer one from container iteration order.

frank_source_refs: implementation alternative, not an accepted FRANK claim
reviews.counterhypothesis: Budget exhaustion is a resource event and may occur while unresolved pressure remains high.
reviews.falsifier: Across representative H1 traces, budget exhaustion always coincides with low residual pressure/error and correct completion.
